stem: What proportion of children with cerebral palsy are estimated to have an intellectual disability?
explanation: Up to 50% is the best estimate for intellectual disability in children with cerebral palsy.
rationale: The estimate is approximately half of affected children, so the option stating up to 50% is correct.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because 10% is too low for the estimated proportion of children with cerebral palsy who have an intellectual disability.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because 25% underestimates the reported proportion, which can be as high as half.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because intellectual disability can affect up to half of children with cerebral palsy.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because 75% is higher than the usual estimate for intellectual disability in cerebral palsy.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because 90% is far above the estimated proportion of children with cerebral palsy who have an intellectual disability.

source.hint: Consider a figure that represents nearly half of the affected population.
